newsitem.title: CHINA: Digital in China network computer pact.
newsitem.headline: Digital in China network computer pact.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp and the state-run China Aerospace Corp signed a preliminary agreement on Tuesday for a possible joint venture to produce and distribute network computers.
Chinese officials at the signing ceremony said they expected a final agreement to be reached later this year calling for a total investment of about $40 million.
Initial shipments of the product were expected early next year, they said.

Digital officials at the ceremony declined to outline the structure of the joint venture company but China Aerospace vice president Xia Guohong told reporters that the firm was likely to be a 50-50 equity venture.
"We are now looking at several sites for production, including Beijing, Tianjin, Shanghai, Suzhou and Zhuhai," said Xia.
Digital will provide engineering and design for the proposed network computer while China Aerospace will supply manufacturing and distribution capability.
The two companies already have a joint venture for the distribution of Digital Equipment workstations.
Digital officials declined to give estimates for demand or initial production for network computers.
"The market will expand. We believe it is sizeable enough to warrant the investment we will be making," said Bobby Choonavala, Digital's Asia Pacific president.

Digital officials said they saw strong demand in China from users who did not need a personal computer but wanted more than a workstation. Lower operating costs would make the product attractive in China, and potential areas included the tax collection agencies and banking system.

The companies said that network computer would be based on the Digital network Appliance Reference Design recently announced by Digital and Network Inc, a unit of Oracle Corp. The reference design is aimed at creating a standard for the network computing platform.
